title: Rollout kinetics failure analysis and safety harness codex
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Summary: During a staged model rollout on 2025-02-07 we observed a repeatable collapse in throughput and a concurrent p95 latency spike after shifting 12-18% traffic to the new variant. The failure pattern differs from prior canary regressions: traffic-burst sensitivity + KV-cache thrashing under mixed-sequence workloads triggered downstream queueing and a slow cascading autoscaling response. Goal: codify reproducible tests, add deterministic safety gates, and build an authorable safety-harness 'codex' (runbook + automation) that prevents rollout kinetic failures without unduly blocking velocity.

Scope and deliverables:
- Detailed failure analysis and hypothesis validation (this ticket).
- Concrete abort/rollback heuristics and thresholds to enforce in the rollout controller.
- Automated synthetic harness that simulates mixed-sequence traffic and KV-cache hit/miss patterns.
- Runbook revisions and a lightweight UI flow for operators to attach rollback reason codes.
- PRs implementing controller-level circuit-breaker and a shadow-replay experiment to validate fixes before canary.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproduction harness that reliably triggers the observed failure locally or in a staging shard within 3 runs.
- Controller abort rules implemented and covered by unit + e2e tests: error-rate delta > 1.2x baseline OR p95 latency up > 30% sustained for 5m triggers abort; also kv-cache miss-rate amplification threshold added.
- Canary policy UI surfaces the abort reason and allows manual override with audit log.
- Post-fix shadow replay for 48h with no recurrence of the collapse under matched traffic profile.
- Runbook written and reviewed by SRE/Runtime/PM with clear oncall play steps and escalation paths.
